issues.item: Triggers: Visual (Uniforms): Military or police uniforms
issues.explanation: For a natural-disaster trauma, military or police uniforms are not an impossible trigger, but in the absence of any disaster-response context elsewhere in the profile they read as a trauma cue more typical of assault, combat, or law-enforcement-related trauma. This makes the trigger set clinically hard to reconcile with the stated trauma type.

issues.item: Threat: Threat in Movements: Sudden movements by others put me immediately on guard
issues.explanation: 'Sudden movements by others put me immediately on guard' implies interpersonal attack vigilance. That threat pattern does not fit well with the rest of the profile, which centers on fragmented disaster memory and non-interpersonal triggers.

issues.item: Triggers: Children Present: Being around children
issues.explanation: For a natural-disaster trauma, 'Being around children' is a hard-to-explain trigger unless the disaster narrative specifically centered on children; nothing else in the profile links children to the trauma, threat, or memory content. This makes the trigger clinically incoherent with the rest of the selected items.

issues.item: Threat: Noticing Weapons: I notice potential weapons or dangerous objects in any environment
issues.explanation: 'Noticing potential weapons or dangerous objects in any environment' implies a violence/assault-related danger schema rather than a natural-disaster threat pattern. It does not fit the other threat items, the disaster trauma type, or the trigger/memory content, which center on flooding, loss of control, and fragmented disaster memories.
